commit message: ♻️ Refactor Packaging and CI (#283) ## Description This PR brings a major refactoring for the overall Python packaging as well as the CI employed in the project. ### Packaging We are (finally) moving away from `setuptools` and towards modern `scikit-build-core` (https://scikit-build-core.readthedocs.io/) This brings many advantages such as  - truly editable installs that also include the C++ part; this implies incredibly fast rebuilds that can be further improved by installing ccache. - completely eliminates the `setup.py` (and the `MANIFEST.in`) file and all custom build code that was required previously. As part of this change, we adopt the established best practice of a src-layout for the Python package. This implies that the Python package no longer lives in the main package directory, but is moved to `src/mqt/...`. This avoids several pitfalls when working with Python packages and makes the overall handling way easier. This also means there is no direct build-time dependency on cmake and ninja anymore as this is automatically handled by scikit-build-core on demand. As part of this rewrite, several `nox` sessions are also updated ### CI MQT Core has introduced reusable workflows in  - https://github.com/cda-tum/mqt-core/pull/396 These have been further refined in  - https://github.com/cda-tum/mqt-core/pull/407 Overall, this allows to  - remove almost all workflow files of this repository - eliminate a lot of maintenance required in this repository to keep up with the latest best practices - rely on dependabot for workflow updates once MQT Core has settled enough so that it follows proper versioning and we can use tags for the workflows here instead of `@main` while at the same time: - having automatic change detection and only triggering jobs that are really necessary; with a single pass check that can be used for branch protection - setting up ccache for all supported workflow jobs which greatly improves compilation times - setting up mold as a better linker under linux - splitting jobs into as many subjobs as possible and feasible to distribute work - automatically creating wheels for all supported platforms (including exotic platforms that need emulation) and Python versions using PyPI trusted publishing - enabling automatic retries for flaky jobs such as MSVC builds or coverage uploads - enabling automatic build parallelization via using Ninja wherever suitable - running an automatic workflow using the minimal versiosn for all Python dependencies to guarantee compatibility As a nice side effect, the new CI has unveiled several issues in the HSF simulator and it's task logic that have subsequently been resolved. Upon writing regression tests, an endianness bug in the Amplitude Mode HSF simulation surfaced. With this PR, the expected results are returned. ## Checklist: <!--- This checklist serves as a reminder of a couple of things that ensure your pull request will be merged swiftly. --> - [x] The pull request only contains commits that are related to it. - [x] I have added appropriate tests and documentation. - [x] I have made sure that all CI jobs on GitHub pass. - [x] The pull request introduces no new warnings and follows the project's style guidelines.

commit message: 🐛 Fix broken `manylinux` wheels (#294) ## Description Due to the way Linux wheels are built by cibuildwheel (in a manylinux docker container), environment varaiables are not passed down to the container. As a result the `CI` environment variable is not defined in the docker container, which is used to flip on the `DEPLOY` CMake setting automatically. This has lead to manylinux wheels being built with `-march=native` that might produce errors like ```console Illegal instruction (core dumped) ``` when trying to import the respective packages. This PR fixes this by making sure that `DEPLOY="ON"` within cibuildwheel. Fixes #288  ## Checklist: <!--- This checklist serves as a reminder of a couple of things that ensure your pull request will be merged swiftly. --> - [x] The pull request only contains commits that are related to it. - [x] I have added appropriate tests and documentation. - [x] I have made sure that all CI jobs on GitHub pass. - [x] The pull request introduces no new warnings and follows the project's style guidelines. commit message: ✨ switch to `mqt-core` Python package (#336) ## Description This PR switches the project to use the newly developed `mqt-core` Python package. Any Python package build will only require the `mqt-core` package as a build and runtime dependency and won't have to rely on fetched version of mqt-core any more. Any regular C++ build will still use the `FetchContent` CMake module. commit message: ⬆️ 👽 Update to mqt-core `v3.0.2` (#538) ## Description This PR adjusts DDSIM so that it works with the latest mqt-core major version. commit message: Makefile now works this way: (*) If an object uses a module, it will depend on module.mod (*) All module objects (modules.o) will be linked at the end;     only the final program depends on them. (*) .o and .mod targets have different rules again; .mod rule     specifies that the .mod file last date of modification     has to be updated (via touch) so as to comply with the     second rule of makefiles and prevent endelss cycles of     recompilation. Lesson: fortran compilers will update the object if the source has been touched but not modified, but it will not update any .mod files that those sources would produce if there is nothing new on them.

author: Chad Hopkins <chopkins@phys.ufl.edu>
commit message: QM/MM AND COULOMB KERNELS NOW USE DOUBLE PRECISION BY DEFAULT The single/mixed precision scheme (calculating prefactors with double precision and doing the rest of the kernel in single precision) which was the default before hasn't been fully validated on long simulations for big systems, so to be safe double is now the default Added compiler flags to turn on mixed precision separately for the QM/MM (qmmm_mp) and Coulomb (coulomb_mp) kernels.  These flags turn on mixed precision only for that kernel, and have no effect, for instance, on the XC code.  The QM/MM and Coulomb kernels should also still obey the full_double option

author: Chad Hopkins <chopkins@phys.ufl.edu>
commit message: Adding visualization options for either the density or a single orbital by generating a .cube format file at the end of SCF The following lio namelist options control cube output: cube_gen   (flag that turns on cube generation at end of SCF)            default: OFF cube_res   (resolution of cube file - corresponds to # of grid             points along longest dimension)            default: 40 cube_sel   (contents of cube file: -1 = density; >0 = MO #)            default: -1 (density) cube_file  (file name to output to)            default: "lio.cube" Cube file generation is slow for high resolutions/large systems on the CPU; this could be ported to GPU using the existing functions/density kernels Added MOD_AMBER compiler flag (commented out by default) that allows basis set keywords/cube file usage via Amber (these require changes to Amber which haven't been added to the Amber tree yet)

author: Chad Hopkins <chopkins@phys.ufl.edu>
commit message: First version of a complete GPU port of the Coulomb energy calculation -Lots of tweaking/optimizing still needed, but it works -Only can do the normal equations/no constraint fit for now -The GPU version calculates the energy integrals on the fly each SCF iteration, so int3mem/s is completely bypassed -Multiple precision does NOT WORK for the fitting calculation (I think this might be due to (or just made worse by) the instability of the normal equations method), so double precision needs to be kept on for now. I've tested multi precision on just the fock kernel, which seems to work fine, so that might be an option in the future

author: Chad Hopkins <chopkins@phys.ufl.edu>
commit message: -To make it easier to persist GPU data for the QM/MM and Coulomb calculations, I'm restructuring that part of the code to be more modular with classes, etc. -Separated the QM/MM and Coulomb code into a separate "analytic_integral" directory.  For now, this code still gets built as part of g2g in terms of Makefiles, but eventually it should be easy to completely separate it with its own Makefile (maybe its own library, as well?) -For right now, the QM/MM and Coulomb calculatations share a lot of common data/code, so mixed precision can't be specified for each of them individually anymore; rather, mixed precision can be turned on for both now with the aint_mp flag. This also meant I had to take out a small optimization to the QM/MM forces code, slowing it down a little, until I get a change to reimplement for both QM/MM and Coulomb. -Mixed precision seems to work OK now for the Coulomb fitting calculation; however, convergence seems to take an extra step or two (sometimes more for the initial density)

author: Francisco <francisco@eneas.(none)>
commit message: linear_algebra module created. The idea is to have all matrix and vector operations go through the generic subroutines of this module, and internal to it are the decisions of how to perform the requested operations. Further development will require to set "interface" modules with libraries (cuda, blas, lapack, magma) to hide those internal manipulations. For example, looking at how matrix_diagon is right now, it would be preferable to have it call generic subroutines "lapack_syevd" or "magma_syevd" that know what kind of version they need to call (dsyevd, rsyevd, etc). Additionally, they might also take care of finding the necessary work array sizes and allocating them.

commit message: Transport 2.0 The next modifications have been made: - Transport now can work with more than 2 electrodes. The number   of electrodes must be declared in the input with the variable   nbias. - Now the electrodes can be activated in a specific moment of TD.   The activation step must be declared in the transport.dat file. - The info of the file atomgroup now must be written it in transport.dat. - Van Voorhis potentials (fockbias_subs) has been updated to work   with transport and Close and Open Shell. The potential for each   atom must be declared in a file called atombias.in.

commit message: (#292) Convergence upgrade  Fixed DIIS for open-shell cases.  Merged linear search into converger_subs.  conver_method (previously conver criter) is now an input variable, although backwards compatibility is available:         conver_method = 1 indicates damping-only (diis = f, hybrid_converg = f).         conver_method = 2 indicates DIIS (diis = t, hybrid_converg = f).         conver_method = 3 indicates hybrid convergence damping/DIIS (hybrid_converg = t)  Included energy-biased DIIS (bDIIS) as a convergence algorithm.         conver_method = 4 enables bDIIS.         conver_method = 5 enables hybrid convergence damping/bDIIS.         DIIS_bias indicates the term by which non-lowest energy terms are multiplied in EMAT.  Included level shifting options:         level_shift indicates whether to use or not level shifting.         lvl_shift_cut indicates the highest HOMO-LUMO gap for which level shifting is enabled.         lvl_shift_en indicates the term added to unnocuppied MOs in the diagonal fock matrix elements.  Included algorithms for EDIIS and ADIIS although they do not work as expected.  Enable a mix of convergence methods:         conver_method = 6 enables mixed strategies, using the maximum DIIS error (max([F,P])) as a criterium.  EDIIS_start indicates the DIIS error at which EDIIS is started.  DIIS_start and bDIIS_start indicate the same for both DIIS and bDIIS. Starting DIIS disables EDIIS and starting bDIIS disables normal DIIS.

commit message: (#364) Add a Github action to run a code linter Adds a Github action that will autocheck code-style in order to have a consistent style across the codebase. This won't affect any forks since it will only run on develop and master branches, so people are free to code as they see fit, but will get a warning if the code doesn't pass the check when they try to merge upstream. For now all languages are disabled (cpp, python, bash, latex) except for yaml in order to not have spurious warnings. Other PRs will format those accordingly and then those languages can be enabled. A fortran linter is not available in this docker image, but might be available in others, so we can try to find one to enable.

author: diegoarmino <12549327+diegoarmino@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message: CMAKE IMPLEMENTATION FOR LIO DESCRIPTION The new CMake implementation is designed to work alongside the old makefile implementation until it seen fit to abandon it at some time in the future. The main goal of the CMake implementation is not so much as to facilitate compilation (it is not any easyier or difficult than before, I believe) but to make the compilation process more transparent and particularly, easier to understand and mantain. The makefile implentation consisted of about 41 makefiles spread about the whole code tree and bearing as complex an interdependence as the code files themselves. All this complexity is hidden now as CMake can, by itself, determine the interdependence of the code files and therefore the order in which they should be compiled, which means that the CMake compilation process is controlled by no more than 12 CMakeLists.txt files (only 4 of which are actually in charge of the compilation of the main code, with the rest belonging to testing and tools compilation). The implementation requires CMake version 3.18 or newer, which is a conservative requirement as Ubuntu 22.04 comes with CMake 3.22 and updating it to an even newer version is very easy to do. CMake compilation is mainly controlled by files named CMakeLists.txt. The implementation consists of one root CMakeLists.txt file, three main ones (one for each of the three main parts of the code: g2g, lioamber and liosolo), a cmake directory containing modules (anciliary files that are normally included into main CMakeLists.txt files) and CMakeLists.txt files for testing and tools compilation. The new CMake compilation option scheme, although preserves the original makefile implementation functionality, differs in its presentation. The new options scheme is more in tune with current CMake good practices, and are thought out to have more descriptive names. A set of previously undocumented options was also added to the main roster alongside comments describing its rough functionality as best I could devise them. The complete set of lio-specific compilation options is defined in the file cmake/ConfigureOptions.cmake. Also the defaults are set identically to the original makefile implementation. MINOR CODE CHANGES A new build_info_cmake.f90 was created as an update of the old build_info.f90. The main task of this file is to log compilation information from the compilation options, so naturally, it had to be recreated to reflect the new CMake option scheme. A new lio_setenv_cmake.sh was added at the root directory that replaces the old liohome.sh script in the case of CMake compilation. The directory tree for the test cases was changed to better automatize its execution. The energy python script in test/energy.py was refactored and updated to make it possible for the user to change the error threshold defaults (which were hardcoded in the original code) as user input to better control the checks precision goals depending of the case. This change was motivated by some tests systematically failing although the differences were actually within acceptable tolerances. Added some comments con g2g/Makefile. Eliminated option for compiler flags for extremely old intel compilers as those are unlikely to ever be used again. Added some comments and caution marks on some undocumented options. In particular fastmath option is allways activated when compiling, but in a way that appears to be uningtentional. Added a comment to highlight this fact. In the CMake implementation this option is part of standard options and documented accordingly. Also comented the undocumented variable subscript_warn. BUGFIXES g2g/init.cpp: Added a precompiler definition to allow for compilation without OpenMP. g2g/regenerate_partition.cpp: Modified to allow for serial compilation (no OpenMP). Changed a print which called an OpenMP function. lioamber/TD.f90: Corrected logic of if() block. CMake compilation does not stop evaluation after (td_eu_step /= 0) is evaluated as false, and causes crash when mod(istep, td_eu_step) is undefined. Corrected the if block making it nested which is a safer option. lioamber/cdft/cdft_utils.f90: Changed "Iteration n°:" for "Iteration No:" as the character ° was not compatible with utf-8 necoding and caused errors in the python scripts in charge of checking test runs. lioamber/converger_subs/converger_ls.f90: Similar changes to cdft_utils.f90. lioamber/fileio/output_scf.f90: Changes in the output format. Changed F12.6 for F14.6 as in some tests energy values would overflow. lioamber/liomain.f90: Changed unsafe if() statement logic. Similar case to that of TD.f90. The evaluation of if ((restart_freq > 0) .and. (MOD(npas, restart_freq) == 0)) did not stop before the "and" if restart_freq=0 and produced a NAN when evaluating the MOD function causing lio to crash. It was rewritten as a nested if which is safer. lioamber/properties/write_population.f90: Similar changes to cdft_utils.f90. test/Makefile: Modified the makefile to reflect the new directory names and script names for tests. test/run_test_external_functionals.py: Modified the script to reflect changes in the directory tree.

author: Lawrence <lawrence@vidriotech.com>
commit message: Added Deflate Levels + Initial Writes to DataPipe DataPipe now support deflate leves before binding.  The normal range is [0,9]. DataPipe considers the special value -1 as disabling compression. Note that the compression isn't set until after export. DataPipe now also supports Initial data writes on export in the event that the user has no intention of appending to the dataset.  To do this, set the data you wish to write in the `data` property of the DataPipe before Exporting. Note that exporting disables `data` property and the data cannot be rewritten without using a speciall overwriting `append` call.

author: Lawrence <lawrence@vidriotech.com>
commit message: Refactoring DataPipe Start DataPipe constructor split into three functions: regular constructor(maxSize, axis) only takes the allocated size and an axis to identify the append axis. data queue fromData(data [, axis]) takes in data and creates a DataPipe from it with the optional axis designation.  If no axis is provided, the assumed axis is the first dimension (in MATLAB order). fromFile(filename, path) returns a DataPipe already bound to the pre-created dataset.  The axis must be set afterwards as the append axis is assumed to be 1. Also added: io.getMatType which does the inverse of io.getBaseType as it takes in a HDF5 tid and returns a MATLAB type name. io.getMatTypeSize which return the size of the type given a MATLAB type name. Draft types.untyped.datapipe.guessChunkSize which, in the future, will implement the h5py method for estimating the best chunk size. Modified: io.parseDataset now updated to use the new fromFile call.

commit message: Fix metaclass failing to write compound references Normally when a reference exists (any ObjectView or RegionView), it is added to the `refs` list and immediately returned. write_base does handle its own reference errors but when it returns, it actually returns back into the export body, which causes errors since an attribute cannot be written if the dataset isn't either. commit message: Fix bugs related to reading logical and enum data types (#758) * Add private props to store dims and type of DataStub These values should ideally be set on construction (they are immutable?) to avoid repeated calls to h5 library * Update parseDataset.m Create DataStub with size and type information available from h5info structure * Update parseDataset.m Add handling for compound data type * Update parseDataset.m Add handling for boolean / logical data type * Update parseDataset.m Include character set value for char type * Improve datatypeInfoToMatlabType Removed 'keyboard' debugging statements and added a default empty output for unresolved types in datatypeInfoToMatlabType. This makes the function safer and avoids unexpected interruptions during execution. * Minor: Fix argument in CheckDtypeTest for map input Corrects the name argument from 'table' to 'map' in the CheckDtypeTest unit test when verifying containers.Map input. * Support and validate HDF5 compound types in DataStub Enhances DataStub and related utilities to handle HDF5 compound types by storing and validating detailed type descriptors as structs. Adds recursive validation for compound type structure in checkDtype, updates getMatType to extract compound type descriptors, and ensures correct handling and error reporting for compound datasets throughout the loading and validation process. * Handle compound HDF5 types in datatypeInfoToMatlabType Added extractCompoundTypeDescriptor to support parsing HDF5 compound types into MATLAB struct type descriptors. This enables correct handling of nested compound, string, enum, and reference types when converting HDF5 datatypes to MATLAB representations. * Set default value for dataType_ property Initialized the private property dataType_ to string.empty in the DataStub class to ensure it has a default value. * Update test to expect struct class for compound type Changed the testTableType unit test to verify that io.getMatType returns a 'struct' class instead of 'table' for H5T_COMPOUND types. This reflects a change in expected behavior as data type of a compound should be represented with a structure instead 'table' char * Update checkDtype.m For numeric types, we should not require strict type match * Update Dataset.m * Improve HDF5 reference type handling in datatype parsing Enhances the datatypeInfoToMatlabType function to explicitly distinguish between 'H5R_OBJECT' and 'H5R_DATASET_REGION' reference types, mapping them to ObjectView and RegionView, respectively. Refactors extractCompoundTypeDescriptor to recursively use datatypeInfoToMatlabType for consistent type detection * Update nwbtest.m * Refactor datatypeInfoToMatlabType to new internal module Moved and refactored the datatypeInfoToMatlabType function from parseDataset.m to +io/+internal/+h5/+datatype/datatypeInfoToMatlabType.m for better modularity and maintainability. Updated parseDataset.m to use the new function location. Removed the old function implementation from parseDataset.m. * Update datatypeInfoToMatlabType.m * Replace error with assert for compound type validation Changed the validation for compound type descriptors from an error to an assert statement in DataStub.m. * Update checkDtype.m Removed unused function Improved errors * Added utility functions for easier use of test schemas in tests * Update dataStubTest.m * Add function to cast values to logical - Added function to cast values read with low-level or high-level h5 functions to logical vectors - Use this new function in io.parseDataset and io.parseCompound * Update parseAttributes.m - Fixed verb from save to read as this function is part of the read pipeline - Fixed bug where utput value was not assigned, leading to error * Update isBool.m - Combine logical expressions using && to break early if condition is not met - Fixes a bug where logical comparison error if Type.Member has a different length than 2 - Added comment about likely bug * Handle enum types in getMatType Updated getMatType to distinguish between boolean and other enum types. Now, if the type is an enum and not a boolean, it returns 'cell' * Update datatypeInfoToMatlabType.m * Add unit tests for enum parsing in io.parseDataset Introduces EnumTest to verify correct parsing of HDF5 enum datasets, including boolean and unknown enum types, in the io.parseDataset and io.parseAttributes functions. Tests cover scalar and array datasets, attribute parsing, and ensure appropriate warnings and data type conversions are handled. * Update EnumTest.m Comment out failed test for coverage reporting * Update parseDataset.m * Refactor enum to logical conversion in HDF5 parsing Replaces direct string comparison with a call to io.internal.h5.cast.toLogical for converting enum values to logicals in both parseAttributes and DataStub. * Add function to convert enum values to cell array of strings Introduces toEnumCellStr, a utility for converting HDF5 enum integer values or cell arrays of strings to a cell array of enum member names, supporting both h5info Datatype structs and H5ML.id type identifiers. Includes helper functions for building enum value-to-name maps from both struct and type ID inputs. * Update enum postprocessing -Fixed bug in toEnumCellStr - Use toEnumCellStr in relevant locations Update test * Renamed "io.internal.h5.cast.toEnumCellStr" to "io.internal.h5.postprocess.toEnumCellStr". * Renamed "io.internal.h5.cast.toLogical" to "io.internal.h5.postprocess.toLogical". * Update toEnumCellStr.m --------- Co-authored-by: Ben Dichter <ben.dichter@gmail.com>

Added the following keywords which trigger reading the next few lines - n_external_field - n_anisotropy - n_interaction_pairs - n_interaction_quadruplets If these are not present the parser looks for external_field_file etc. instead. In the files the parser uses, it looks for the n_external_field etc. keywords. commit message: Core: split Simulation API into Start and Stop, improved SingleShot. Now, both regular and single-shot simulations will run until they are stopped (e.g. with Simulation_Stop) or Iteration is called while some condition is not fulfilled. Single-shot iterations can be triggered with Simulation_SingleShot, but only after Simulation_Start_SingleShot has been called. With this mechanism, the performance of single-shot simulations should increase significantly, as the Method class does not have to be re-instantiated at every iteration. Updated unit tests accordingly. Also updated ControlWidget accordingly. Also added State validity checks to API calls, mainly via the from_indices function. Also fixed setup.py, which did not always determine the git commit datetime correctly.

author: G. P. Mueller <gpmueller@outlook.com>
commit message: Core: bugfixes for removing systems from the chain. The issue probably existed due to the somewhat unclear names `Simulation_Running_On_Chain` (checks chain only) and `Simulation_Running_On_Image` (checks specified image only, not checking for simulations running on the entire chain), which are mutually exclusive. When removing systems from a chain, running calculations may need to be stopped beforehand. So far, the checks were incomplete, in particular when calculations on individual images were running (which were therefore not stopped). The method could still hold a shared pointer to the image and continue running, meaning the GUI thread controlling the calculation could stall the GUI. It seems these bugs were avoided in the Qt GUI by placing additional checks around the API calls, which should not be needed. Note, when increasing the chain length, one only needs to check that no calculation is running across the whole chain.

commit message: HTST: Implementation of sparse HTST computations. Can be found in new header file and used by giving the `sparse=True` argument to the `calculate` api function. Overall, the sparse implementation greatly reduces the memory footprint and improves the computation speed as long as the number of interaction partners per spin is low (which is almost always the case if no DDI is present). In the sparse implementation no eigenvalues or eigenvectors are explicitly calculated, which means the `get_eigenvectors` and `get_eigenvalues` API functions cannot be used in conjunction with it. The old (dense) implementation of HTST has been left untouched, as it could potentially still be useful when DDI is involved or when all eigenvalues/vectors are needed.

commit message: Bugfix in Core: deadlock in `OrderedLock` class. If a second thread called `lock` and was waiting on `cvar.back()`, the referenced `std::condition_variable` could be destructed by the first locking thread calling `unlock`, causing the second thread to `wait` forever. This is fixed by `pop`ing the queue only after `wait` completed (i.e. within `lock`). Additionally, spurious wakeups could cause the `wait` to end prematurely, which is fixed by using the predicated overload. Also made some naming improvements and fixed formatting.

commit message: Core: overhaul `Filter_File_Handle` The handle contained unused or unnecessary functions, exposed its internal string-stream and had some unnecessarily confusing naming. In order not to introduce a huge amount of changes throughout the entire codebase, the general idea is kept the same:  - the handle throws if a file cannot be opened  - the user manipulates the file stream by calling searching functions,    like `Find` or `Read_String` and subsequently streams out of the    handle, `file_handle >> variable`. This allows the user to flexibly    control what happens when a given keyword was found. The code should now be a little easier to understand and further improve in the future. Aside from the above, more things are now `const` and properly initialized upon construction. Also made a few minor quality improvements in a few places.

commit message: refactor(modular Hamiltonian): connect Interaction::Gaussian data Introduces the data structure for storing interactions. It is of type: `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Engine::Interaction::ABC>>` This vector marks the `Hamiltonian` as the owner of the interactions and necessitates the creation of constructors according to the rule of five. For setting and getting the interactions a set of templated member functions is used which can also be used at run time given the name of the interaction. The Gaussian interaction is not usable with this commit.

commit message: refactor(`TableParser`): centralize common logic for parsing data tables flexible parsing of table data whose column order isn't known at compile time has lead to a lot of code duplication. The `TableParser` class fixes that by putting the logic for reading the rows of this type of table in a single place. The `parse` method allows specifying how the data from each row should be transformed before it is stored. author: puerling <t.puerling@fz-juelich.de>
commit message: enhancement(API): less greedy resize of spin vectors trough the API Previously the vectors containing atom local quantities were updated whenever there was any change to the geometry. That means that any change to the geometry (like setting `mu_s`) invalidates the pointer to these quantities, like the pointer returned by `Configuration_Get_Spin_Directions()`. For `mu_s` this is unexpected, because it requires deep knowledge of implementation details. This commit therefore adds a check whether a resize is necessary, by checking whether the size described by two geometry objects is the same and only does a resize if they differ. This should result in more intuitive behaviour when it comes to changing quantities that are related with the geometry through our implementation.

commit message: fix unconstrained Metropolis trial algorithm and unify call signatures This fix restores the Markov property of the unconstrained Metropolis trial algorithm. Before hitting the same spin twice in a single iteration would restore the state of the spin to the state before the first hit whether the first trial move has been accepted or not. This breaks the Markov property of the trial moves, because the outcome of the second trial move for a doubly hit spin depends on the outcome of the first hit. Additionally, this commit unifies the call signatures of the constrained and unconstrained Metropolis algorithms.

commit message: feature: semi-classical Monte Carlo sampling This implements a semi-classical Monte Carlo trial move. Semi-classical here means that there is an integer spin quantum number `spin_qn` that restricts the component along the local effective field to be on one of the `spin_qn + 1` level sets in [-1, 1]. That means that `spin_qn` relates to the conventional spin quantum number s by `s = spin_qn / 2`.

commit message: refactor(toml_config): unified vector parsing Unifies the implementation and config file interface for parsing vectors. If it is a 'true' vector, like the temperature gradient or the external field each vector can be specified either as an array, or as a table with fields 'direction' and 'magnitude'. The vector is then internally stored in terms of these two quantities. If it is a quantity that has an associated normalized vector and a magnitude, like the uniaxial anisotropy the fields are 'normal' and 'magnitude'. This time also both have to be provided, because there is ambiguity in how the magnitude might be determined from the norm of the provided vector. This skips the `stt_magnitude` and `stt_polarization_direction` fields, because those should be adapted to be more understandable.

commit message: Fixed memory allocation bugs: no space for biases Memory was allocated without space for biases. As the result of this some gradients were overwritten by weights, and some costs were overwritten by gradients. You can see below that word vector positions inside W are calculated with additional space for bias, for example "l1 = (cr.word1 - 1LL) * (vector_size + 1)". Thus the memory allocation must also use additional space. With this fix applied the algorithm tends to perform slightly better on provided analogy tests.

author: Christopher Manning <manning@cs.stanford.edu>
commit message: Enhance token reading. Previously, if a  token was too long, then when it was truncated, a UTF-8 encoded unicode character could be split, resulting in invalid UTF-8 strings in the vocabulary. Now, truncation only occurs at what would be the end of a valid UTF-8 encoded character. (But this won't do much harm if the encoding is different.) Also, token reading is the same between vocab_count and cooccur, whereas before inconsistencies could occur. Morever, if there was no end of line at eof, cooccurrences with the last word used to be lost. Now they aren't.

This led t `vocab_size = 0`, which caused a segfault during execution. I've raised an error if the vocab size is still 0 after trying to read the vocab file. This seems a bit better than checking for a directory, since we still should raise if an incorrect but existing file path was passed.
